chunks: From him, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding a man who struck another man in the ear with a bone, and the victim claimed that he could not hear, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is placed under surveillance and tested (for hearing), and awaited for one year. If he hears, or two men testify against him that he can hear, then otherwise he is made to swear an oath, and he is given the blood money (diya).'

It was said, 'O Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him)! What if it is discovered afterwards that he can hear?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, returns his hearing, I do not see any liability upon him.'

key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: Blood money or financial compensation for injury or death
key_terms.يُسْتَغْفَلُ: Tested or examined (specifically for hearing in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on compensating for an ear injury when the victim claims permanent deafness?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the jurisprudential principle of 'taraṣṣud' (surveillance/observation) to verify the permanence of injury before finalizing diya, reflecting the Shia emphasis on empirical verification in legal rulings. It highlights the distinction between temporary and permanent damage, ensuring that compensation is neither excessive nor insufficient, thereby upholding justice in financial liabilities. The ruling underscores the importance of waiting for a full year to confirm the stability of the condition, a standard practice in Islamic medical jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: From him, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, both together from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Suleyman Bin Khalid,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said with regards to a man who struck a man in his ear with a bone, so he claimed that he cannot hear. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be placed under surveillance and would be awaited with for a year. So if he hears, or two men testify against him that he can hear, or else he would be made to swear an oath, and he would be given the wergild’.

It was said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>! So if it was discovered afterwards that he can hear?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Returns his hearing, I<sup>asws</sup> do not see anything upon him’.
